zh.title: 民航局罰臺灣虎航20萬元 因A320發動機過期檢查
zh.summary: 民航局罰臺灣虎航20萬元；虎航自主發現並通報完成檢查
body: 交通部民用航空局於10月27日公佈最新違規裁罰資訊，指出臺灣虎航一架A320-271N客機（註冊號B-50023）二號發動機燃燒室缺點檢查管制逾期，依民航法處以新臺幣20萬元罰鍰，並要求立即改善。
臺灣虎航回應指出，該機於去年9月執行航班調度時出現管制時間計算落差，經落實安全管理系統（SMS）自主查覈發現後，當日第一時間完成發動機檢查並確認符合安全規範，同時主動向民航局提報。
航空公司表示，飛航安全向來視為不可妥協的最高原則，針對此事件已全面深刻檢討並進行改善，且已加強雙重覆核機制，嚴格杜絕類似情事再次發生。
民航局表示，定期會在官網更新違規事件裁罰資訊，以利社會大眾查閱。

en.title: CAA fines Tigerair Taiwan NT$200,000 over overdue A320 engine inspection
en.summary: CAA fines Tigerair Taiwan NT$200k; airline self‑reported overdue engine check
body: The Civil Aeronautics Administration (CAA) announced on 27 October 2026 that Tigerair Taiwan was fined NT$200,000 after an A320‑271N (registration B-50023) was found to have an overdue inspection of the number‑two engine combustion chamber, in violation of the Civil Aviation Act, and was ordered to rectify the issue immediately.

Tigerair Taiwan responded that the aircraft experienced a timing‑calculation discrepancy during flight scheduling in September 2025; the discrepancy was discovered through the airline’s Safety Management System (SMS) self‑audit, after which the engine inspection was completed the same day and the finding was voluntarily reported to the CAA.

The carrier emphasized that flight safety remains its non‑negotiable top principle, stating that it has conducted a comprehensive review, implemented corrective actions, and strengthened a dual‑check mechanism to prevent recurrence.
The CAA regularly updates its online database of violation penalties, and this notice represents the latest enforcement action against a domestic carrier for engine‑maintenance non‑compliance.

zh.title: 空中巴士 A350-900ULR 航程達 9,700 海里，靠移除部件而非加裝燃油箱
zh.summary: A350-900ULR 以移除部件達成 9,700 海里航程；Simple Flying 報導
body: 空中巴士 A350-900ULR 的航程達到 9,700 海里，據 Simple Flying 報導，這項極致航程並非靠額外燃油箱，而是通過移除部件實現。
報導指出，通常增加航程意味著需要更多燃油。
並說明 A350-900ULR 的卓越航程歸功於遠不止於加裝燃油的設計變更。
文章強調航程提升是因為移除部件，而非加裝額外燃油箱。
該文於 2026 年 10 月 26 日由 Simple Flying 發布。

en.title: Airbus A350-900ULR reaches 9,700 NM range by removing parts, not adding fuel tanks
en.summary: A350-900ULR achieves 9,700 NM range via component removal; Simple Flying reports
body: The Airbus A350-900ULR achieves a range of 9,700 nautical miles, according to Simple Flying, and this extreme range comes from removing components rather than adding extra fuel tanks.
The summary notes that typically more range means more fuel is needed.
It adds that for the A350-900ULR the exceptional range is thanks to far more than just added fuel.
The article explains that the range increase comes because parts were removed, not extra fuel tanks.
The piece was published on 26 October 2026.
Simple Flying released the report on 26 October 2026.

zh.title: 芬蘭航空開航赫爾辛基－墨爾本每日A350班機 經曼谷
zh.summary: 芬蘭航空首航赫爾辛基至墨爾本經曼谷每日A350班機
body: 芬蘭航空已啟動每日往返赫爾辛基機場（HEL）與墨爾本機場（MEL）的航線，經由曼谷素萬那普機場（BKK），這是該航空公司首次將澳洲納入自有定期航線網絡。
首航班機 AY145 於 2026 年 10 月 25 日凌晨 01:15（當地時間）從赫爾辛基起飛，使用空中巴士 A350-900（註冊號 OH-LWO），預計於 10 月 26 日 07:20 抵達墨爾本，全程約 22 小時 5 分鐘。
該航線全年運行，在曼谷停留不到兩小時；乘客全程乘坐同一架飛機，但需在經停時離開客艙，並可單獨預訂赫爾辛基─曼谷或曼谷─墨爾本航段。
芬蘭航空表示選擇墨爾本是因其全年皆具備休閒與商務需求，擁有龐大歐洲僑民、留學生與外派勞工羣體，能提供穩定載客率。
曼谷經停主要受限於飛機航程與機組值勤時限；乘客續飛墨爾本時需攜帶手提行李下機接受安檢，並依澳洲要求再次查驗旅證與手提行李。

en.title: Finnair launches daily A350 service Helsinki–Melbourne via Bangkok
en.summary: Finnair starts daily A350 Helsinki‑Melbourne flights via Bangkok
body: Finnair has launched daily flights between Helsinki Airport (HEL) and Melbourne Airport (MEL) via Bangkok’s Suvarnabhumi Airport (BKK), adding Australia to its own scheduled network for the first time.

The inaugural flight, AY145, departed Helsinki on October 25, 2026, at 01:15 local time on an Airbus A350‑900 registered OH‑LWO. It was scheduled to arrive in Melbourne at 07:20 local time on October 26, after a total journey of 22 hours and five minutes.

The year‑round service includes a stopover of just under two hours in Bangkok. Passengers stay with the same aircraft for the whole journey but must leave the cabin during the stop, and each sector can also be booked on its own, giving Finnair access to the Thailand‑Australia market through its Bangkok‑Melbourne flights.

Finnair said it chose Melbourne after looking for a long‑haul destination that could sustain demand all year, citing the city’s mix of leisure and business travel, its large European community, and its international students and expatriate workers.

The Bangkok stop is needed because of both the aircraft’s range and crew duty limits. Passengers continuing to Melbourne leave the aircraft with all their hand luggage and go through security screening before returning to the gate, where their travel documents and hand luggage are checked again under Australian requirements.
